subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage: After lunch break in the Class 6 corridor, the vase lay in pieces and Mrs. Iyer was asking who did it. Nitin saw Hafsa look at the floor. "It was Nitin," said someone, and Hafsa said nothing. Nitin took the blame, and his eyes stung. That evening, in the school van, he said, "Hafsa, I saw you knock it." She flushed and whispered, "I was scared of my father." Nitin looked out of the window for a while. "I was hurt," he said. "I want to hear more, but I do not know yet if we are friends the same way."

qa.q: What lay in pieces in the corridor?
Why did Nitin's eyes sting when he took the blame?
qa.a: He felt betrayed, because he had seen Hafsa knock the vase and she let him carry the blame.

qa.q: What did Nitin do that avoided revenge and left room for repair?
qa.a: He told Hafsa what he had seen, listened to her reason and said he needed time to decide about the friendship.

qa.q: How might Hafsa have felt in the van when Nitin spoke?
qa.a: Hafsa probably felt ashamed and afraid, and she may have wanted to explain why she stayed silent.

grounding: A child takes blame that a friend let fall on him; he tells her what he saw, hears her out and decides slowly about repairing trust.

subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage: In Class 6, Kalyani and I were caught near the broken science-lab window. I'm Farhan. It was Kalyani's ball that broke it, but when Sir asked, she said nothing. She just looked at me. I got a note home and had to miss football for a week. I lay awake feeling as if something inside had cracked. For three days I didn't speak to her. Then I made myself say it. 'Kalyani, I saw you stay quiet. You let me take it.' Her eyes filled. 'I was scared I'd be dropped from the sports team. I'm sorry.' I listened. I understood a bit. But I didn't say 'It's fine,' because it wasn't. I told her I needed time. It took most of the term before I trusted her again.

qa.q: How long did Farhan have to miss football?
How did Farhan feel lying awake?
qa.a: Betrayed and hurt, as if something inside had cracked.
Told Kalyani plainly what had been seen, listened to her reason, and took time before trusting her again.

qa.q: Why did Kalyani stay quiet, according to her?
qa.a: She was scared of being dropped from the sports team, and she felt sorry afterwards.

grounding: A child whose friend let them take the blame tells her so, hears her out, and rebuilds trust slowly.

subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
passage:
Class teacher's note, by Manjula Rao, Friday.
This morning I found chalk drawings all over the new board and, after a quick look, sent Ganga to the office because she was standing nearest. At lunch Ganga came back to me, very quietly. She said her friend Meghna had made the drawings and let Ganga take the blame. Ganga's hands were clenched and her voice shook: 'She saw them take me and didn't say anything.' I asked Meghna, who admitted it and cried. I apologised to Ganga for not checking. Ganga told Meghna, 'I saw what you did,' and listened to her reason. She did not hug her. She told me she would decide about the friendship 'later, maybe'. I think that is wise.

qa.q: What did Ganga's clenched hands and shaking voice show?
qa.a: She felt deeply betrayed and angry that Meghna watched her take the blame.

qa.q: How did Ganga handle Meghna afterwards?
qa.a: She told Meghna she saw what she did, listened to her reason, and chose to decide about the friendship slowly.

qa.q: How might Meghna feel after admitting it?
qa.a: Ashamed and sorry; she cried when asked.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a girl betrayed by a friend who let her take the blame, facing the friend and deciding slowly about trust.
